title: 2026 environmental-permit compliance, climate-impact and scoring QA controls

sources.title: Waste operations and installations: assessing and scoring environmental permit compliance
Environmental permits: when and how you are charged

facts.source_fact: The waste-operations and installations compliance-scoring guide was updated on 5 June 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Carry the current compliance-policy vintage with scoring records.

facts.source_fact: The guide applies to permit holders for waste operations and installations, including intensive farming.
facts.expected_handling: Check regulated-activity scope before applying scoring logic.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency describes its permit regulation approach as consistent, transparent and proportionate.
facts.expected_handling: Retain policy-purpose context when interpreting scores.

facts.source_fact: The guide defines six principles for assessing and scoring permit compliance.
facts.expected_handling: Do not reduce the assessment framework to a single numeric score.

facts.source_fact: Compliance Assessment Report forms record all non-compliances identified during an assessment and are provided to the permit holder and placed on the public register as required.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve CAR provenance and public-record status.

facts.source_fact: The Environment Agency generally categorises and scores non-compliances that relate directly to permit conditions.
facts.expected_handling: Separate recorded non-compliances from score-eligible permit-condition breaches.

facts.source_fact: The compliance year runs from 1 January to 31 December.
facts.expected_handling: Aggregate scores within the correct compliance year.

facts.source_fact: The annual non-compliance score affects the site's compliance band and subsistence fee.
facts.expected_handling: Keep operational compliance score and financial consequence linked but distinct.

facts.source_fact: The CAR framework includes emissions to air, land and groundwater, surface water, sewer and waste as compliance sub-criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Attach the relevant emissions medium to each recorded issue.

facts.source_fact: The CAR framework separately includes monitoring of emissions/environment, records, maintenance, reporting and notification.
facts.expected_handling: Do not merge measurement-quality failures with emission-limit breaches without the permit basis.

facts.source_fact: Compliance assessments vary in frequency, duration, detail and complexity based on activity scale and likelihood of non-compliance.
facts.expected_handling: Avoid inferring equal inspection intensity across sites.

facts.source_fact: Non-compliances relating to an individual permit condition are generally consolidated to one category and score during an assessment, with special treatment for emission-limit-value non-compliances.
facts.expected_handling: Prevent double-counting consolidated permit-condition scores.

facts.source_fact: Regular emission-limit-value non-compliance is consolidated per ELV per compliance-year quarter.
facts.expected_handling: Use ELV and quarter identifiers when aggregating scores.

facts.source_fact: Risk categorisation reflects the reasonably foreseeable impact on human health, quality of life and the environment, except amenity conditions use actual impact.
facts.expected_handling: Carry impact basis and receptor context with the category.

facts.source_fact: Compliance assessments identify and score root causes, often linked to management-system deficiencies.
facts.expected_handling: Store original non-compliance and root-cause findings separately.

facts.source_fact: In qualifying circumstances scores may be suspended while active corrective steps are taken, for a maximum of six months.
facts.expected_handling: Record suspension start, basis and expiry rather than deleting the score.

facts.source_fact: The guide defines four risk categories scored at 60, 31, 4 and 0.1 points respectively.
facts.expected_handling: Store both category and points using the current policy version.

facts.source_fact: For certain non-routine greenhouse-gas releases, the Environment Agency also considers wider and longer-term climate-change impact when assessing risk.
facts.expected_handling: Flag climate-impact consideration without converting it into a parcel emission measurement.

facts.source_fact: CAR forms are usually sent within 14 days; permit holders can raise concerns within 14 calendar days and can request a regulatory-decision appeal within the stated 28-day window after the response.
facts.expected_handling: Carry assessment, receipt, challenge and appeal dates separately.

facts.source_fact: Compliance bands A to F are derived from annual scores and are used to adjust subsistence charges; the charging guidance was updated on 1 April 2026.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the applicable compliance-year band and current charge guidance together.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach permit type, condition, emissions medium and compliance-year scope before downstream use.
Attach assessment date, compliance year, policy update and charge vintage.
Carry CAR, category, points, consolidation, suspension and appeal provenance.
Do not convert compliance scores or climate-impact governance into a parcel-level measured emission without a separate parcel-binding gate.
